classification.difficultyReason: Use the hinted quadrilateral decomposition and generalise triangulation to the heptagon angle sum.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By dividing the quadrilateral below into two triangles, show that the angle sum in a quadrilateral is $360^\circ$

spec.description: Unshaded irregular convex quadrilateral A–B–C–D, with external labels and no diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Four perimeter edges; B highest, C rightmost, D below A. Coordinates reconstruct schematic placement and do not assert measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Question perimeter and labels only; diagonal belongs to the response.

answer.worked:
Draw diagonal $AC$, forming triangles $ABC$ and $ACD$. Each triangle has angle sum $180^\circ$. Their angles together form all four interior angles of the quadrilateral.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Quadrilateral angle sum}&=180^\circ+180^\circ\\&=360^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: The supplied quadrilateral with diagonal AC added.
spec.mathematics: AC partitions the convex quadrilateral into exactly two triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution-only diagonal; complete base figure retained.

inlines.text: A heptagon is a seven-sided figure, as shown below.
What is the angle sum of a heptagon?

spec.description: Unlabelled, unshaded convex heptagon with an approximately vertical right edge.
spec.mathematics: Seven vertices and seven edges. Regularity is not asserted. No diagonals or measurements are supplied.

answer.worked:
Split the heptagon into five triangles by drawing four diagonals from one vertex. Each triangle has angle sum $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Heptagon angle sum}&=180^\circ\times5\\&=900^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Source heptagon with four solution-only diagonals from its highest vertex.
spec.mathematics: The four noncrossing diagonals partition the convex heptagon into five triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed triangulation appears only in the solution.
